lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.v: Long-term debt ₹553 cr vs working capital ₹1,537 cr
ch.w: Graham wanted the short-term cushion alone to be able to repay long-term loans.

ch.n: A profit every year for 10 years

ch.v: Profit in all 4 yrs we have

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years
ch.r: EPS +33% over 10 years (3-year averages at each end)
ch.w: EPS (average of the first 2 vs last 2 years we have) moved -8%.

story.what_it_does: Hexaware is an IT services company that earned about USD 1.5 billion in revenue in CY25, with roughly 34,000 employees. It sells technology services to large clients, and its top 5 customers made up about 25% of revenue recently.
story.plans: Management aims to launch one new service every month and to build AI skills, with a goal of 1,000 Anthropic-certified staff and AI architects by mid next year. It is also restructuring its Netherlands operations and reviewing its strategy after a leadership change.
story.moat: The notes do not describe a clear competitive moat. Client spread has improved, with the top 5 share falling to 24.7%, and attrition is steady near 11%, but the company itself flags AI as a top risk that could shrink existing service revenue.

scenarios.story: Delayed large deals start ramping and the weak GSE client headwind fades, so growth speeds up from the 4% range. Margins improve through the year as the Netherlands restructuring and new AI services help.
signals_to_watch: Constant-currency revenue growth rising above the 4.5% seen in Q3 CY26
Adjusted EBIT margin moving back toward the 13.0%-14.0% range after one-off items fade

scenarios.story: Growth stays in the mid-single digits, with a seasonal dip in Q4 and a margin near 13%-13.5% for the full year. The company works through its strategy review without a big change in direction.
signals_to_watch: Outlook given with the full-year results, since none was given for Q4 CY26
Adjusted EBIT margin staying within the 13%-13.5% full-year range

scenarios.story: AI cuts the scope of renewals, and large deal decisions keep slipping because of the macro and Middle East conflict. Guidance has already been cut and then dropped, so further disappointments could follow.
signals_to_watch: Further revenue misses versus management's own expectations because of the GSE client and slow large deals
Receivables and unbilled revenue rising faster than revenue, as seen from INR 25,431 Mn to INR 33,177 Mn
